questions.q: What is a REST client primarily used for?
options: Writing and deploying integration code
Building, sending, and inspecting HTTP requests directly, without code
Storing financial transactions permanently
Replacing the need for authentication
questions.explain: A REST client is a tool for directly testing HTTP requests.

questions.q: Why would a consultant test a call in a REST client before it's wired into an integration tool?
options: To verify the call works and see the real response shape before anything depends on it
To avoid needing documentation at all
Because REST clients are required by Oracle to use the API at all
To permanently delete test data
questions.explain: Testing first catches problems before a real integration relies on the call.

questions.q: What is the benefit of setting authentication at the collection level instead of per request?
options: It makes requests slower
It disables the Accept header
Every request in the collection automatically reuses the same credentials
It is required by HTTP and has no practical benefit
questions.explain: Collection-level auth means you configure credentials once and every saved request reuses them.

questions.q: What is a 'variable' like {{base}} useful for in a saved request?
options: Encrypting the request body
Deleting the resource automatically
Changing the HTTP method
Letting the same saved request point at a different environment (test vs. production) without rewriting it
questions.explain: Variables let one request template work across multiple environments.

questions.q: Why save a working request as a named test case rather than discarding it after use?
options: Saved requests are required by Oracle for billing purposes
It becomes reusable documentation for troubleshooting the same integration later
It automatically fixes any future errors
There is no benefit to saving requests
questions.explain: A saved request becomes a repeatable reference for later troubleshooting.
